methods.name: Closest prices
methods.plain: Pairs whose prices moved closest last year; bet any gap closes.

methods.name: Cointegration
methods.plain: Pairs whose gap passed a statistical test for staying stable, and closes fast.

methods.name: Moving hedge
methods.plain: Cointegrated pairs with a hedge ratio updated every day.

methods.name: PCA leftovers
methods.plain: Each asset against the market's main forces; bet the leftover snaps back.

leaderboard.name: Named stock pairs, moving hedge
leaderboard.verdict_plain: Some signs of a real effect, too small to rely on.

leaderboard.name: Industry pairs, closest prices
leaderboard.description: Every six months, picks the five industry pairs within the same sector whose prices moved closest over the past year, and bets on any gap of two standard deviations closing, as Gatev, Goetzmann and Rouwenhorst did with stocks. Their profits shrank after the 1990s.
leaderboard.verdict_plain: Makes a little, but no more than chance would after this many tries.

leaderboard.name: Linked industries, cointegrated
leaderboard.description: The same test on 25 industry pairs chosen by hand for a business link, such as soft drinks against beer. Fewer pairs, so fewer chances to find one by luck, and fewer trades.
leaderboard.verdict_plain: Loses money after costs. Nothing to rely on.

leaderboard.name: Named stock pairs, cointegrated
leaderboard.verdict_plain: Loses money after costs. Nothing to rely on.

leaderboard.name: Stock pairs, cointegrated
leaderboard.verdict_plain: Loses money after costs. Nothing to rely on.

leaderboard.name: Linked industries, moving hedge
leaderboard.description: Hand-picked industry pairs that pass the cointegration test, traded on a hedge ratio that a Kalman filter updates every day. Adapts to slow drift; can also chase noise.
leaderboard.verdict_plain: Loses money after costs. Nothing to rely on.

leaderboard.name: Stock leftovers (PCA)
leaderboard.verdict_plain: Loses money after costs. Nothing to rely on.

leaderboard.name: Industry pairs, cointegrated
leaderboard.description: Every six months, tests every same-sector industry pair for a stable gap (Engle and Granger), keeps those whose gaps halve within 60 days, and trades the five strongest. A pair can stop being one; a gap past four standard deviations closes the trade.
leaderboard.verdict_plain: Loses money after costs. Nothing to rely on.

leaderboard.name: Stock pairs, closest prices
leaderboard.verdict_plain: Loses money after costs. Nothing to rely on.

leaderboard.name: Industry leftovers (PCA)
leaderboard.description: Explains each industry's daily moves by the three main market-wide forces, then bets that the part left over snaps back, as Avellaneda and Lee did with stocks. Hedged against those forces. Their profits fell after 2003 and it lost hard in August 2007.
leaderboard.verdict_plain: Loses money after costs. Nothing to rely on.
